colleges.title: College map: New York, New Jersey and Pennsylvania
colleges.row_unit: One institution (UNITID) in the College Scorecard October 15, 2026 most-recent-cohorts snapshot.
colleges.selection: STABBR in NY/NJ/PA; CURROPER = 1; PREDDEG = 3 (predominantly bachelor-degree granting). All matching institutions retained, including missing measures. This is a geographic teaching subset, not a ranking or representative national sample.

college_id.meaning: Stable IPEDS institution identifier; not a rank.

latitude.meaning: Reported institution location; missing coordinates stay blank and cannot be mapped.

longitude.meaning: Reported institution location; negative values west of Greenwich.

annual_net_price.source: NPT4_PUB for public; NPT4_PRIV for private
annual_net_price.meaning: Average cost of attendance minus grants and scholarships for full-time, first-time undergraduates receiving Title IV aid. Public colleges use in-state students. It is an observed group average, not a personalized quote, sticker tuition, or necessarily the price for an out-of-state applicant.

completion_rate.period: Fall 2019 or academic year 2019–20 entry cohort; reported in 2025–26
completion_rate.meaning: First-time, full-time degree/certificate-seeking cohort completing at the institution within 150% of normal program time (typically six years for a bachelor degree). Does not describe all students or personal chances.

data_release.meaning: Snapshot release date, not the observation year of every measure.

colleges.missing_policy: NA, NULL, PrivacySuppressed or empty source values become null in JSON and empty fields in CSV. Never zero-fill. Price conditions omit missing prices; show the missing count separately. One row has no coordinates and remains in table/filter counts.
limits: No major offerings or admission-rank data are included.
State and institution-type summaries are unweighted institution summaries, not student-level estimates.
Net price and completion concern different cohorts; the release combines multiple reporting periods.

majors.title: National outcomes by undergraduate major
majors.selection: All 73 named major categories; the source Overall aggregate is excluded to avoid treating it as an additional major.
majors.row_unit: One undergraduate-major category, nationally aggregated; not a college or an individual.
majors.source_notes: Notes: Figures are for 2024. Unemployment and underemployment rates are for recent college graduates (that is, those aged 22 to 27 with a bachelor's degree or higher), and median wages are for full-time workers with a bachelor's degree only. Early career graduates are those aged 22 to 27, and mid-career graduates are those aged 35 to 45. Graduate degree share is based on the adult working-age population (that is, those aged 25 to 65) with a bachelor's degree or higher. All figures exclude those currently enrolled in school. Data are updated annually at the beginning of each calendar year.
majors.source: Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey (IPUMS).
majors.wage_population: Full-time workers with a bachelor degree only, not currently enrolled; early career ages 22–27 and mid-career ages 35–45.
majors.rate_population: Recent graduates ages 22–27 with a bachelor degree or higher, not currently enrolled.
majors.graduate_degree_population: Working-age adults ages 25–65 with a bachelor degree or higher, not currently enrolled.
majors.underemployment_definition: Working in a job that typically does not require a college degree; this does not mean unemployed or necessarily low paid.
majors.currency: US dollars, annual median wage in 2024
limits: Two age groups are different people observed in the same year, not a tracked salary-growth path.
Medians are not a salary range or individual forecast. These data do not identify the causal effect of choosing a major.
National major categories cannot be joined directly to this college shortlist or used to infer offered programs.
This dataset has bachelor-major categories; it does not compare all career pathways or professional training durations.

ai.title: Reported business AI use: selected sectors and national reference
ai.row_unit: One sector estimate or the national all-businesses reference for the same survey period.
ai.measure: Share of surveyed businesses reporting AI use in any business function during the preceding two weeks.
ai.scope: Two selected sectors plus a national reference, transcribed from precise published estimates in the Census article. The approximate Retail Trade value is intentionally omitted.
limits: Business adoption is not the percentage of jobs lost, worker use, exposure, or a forecast for a college major.
The national reference includes sectors; these three rows are not disjoint pieces and must not be added.
Point estimates are descriptive here; no confidence-interval or significance test is reconstructed.
The question wording changed on November 17, 2025. Do not splice these estimates into the earlier goods/services-use series as if comparable.
This is a dated May 2026 snapshot, not the latest available BTOS release.

geometry.title: 2025 Census state cartographic boundaries at 1:20,000,000
geometry.scope: Contiguous 48 states plus District of Columbia; Alaska, Hawaii and territories omitted from this regional teaching-map basemap.
geometry.coordinate_system: Source NAD83 geographic longitude/latitude; used for generalized display only.
geometry.limits: Generalized geographic display; not for address geocoding, exact boundaries, distance or area measurement.
